parsed.use_case: A photo editor can rotate a square image directly in its pixel buffer, avoiding a second full-sized buffer when memory is constrained. The same operation appears when reorienting square tiles in a graphics or image-processing pipeline.
system_examples: Image-processing libraries — rotate square pixel buffers in place when their APIs or constrained workflows avoid allocating a second image.
Embedded graphics systems — reorient square display or icon buffers while limiting temporary memory use.
parsed.explanation: The standard in-place method performs a transpose followed by reversing each row, taking O(n²) time and O(1) extra space. A straightforward copy-based rotation also takes O(n²) time but needs O(n²) additional space; avoiding that allocation matters for large images or memory-limited devices. The exact in-place constraint is mostly an algorithm exercise, since many production image APIs use separate output buffers for simpler and safer processing.
